Previously: 2026-05-07. Drift-check script extension references updated **`.mjs`** → **`.ts`** per DEC-20260507-A; Rule 13 drift-detection bullets reworded to reflect that drift-check substrate now imports from **`platform-facts.ts`** canonical rather than carrying inline static maps. Previously: 2026-05-05 (Payee Assurance → Counterparty Assurance rename per DEC-20260502-A). 2026-04-20 (Products/Infrastructure split per DEC-20260420-E/F/H — 9 sections instead of 8, Products section reserved for vertical products, Infrastructure section added for substrate pages, Competitive Landscape archived, Feature Registry moved to Infrastructure).* **This page is the entry point for anyone — human or assistant — who needs to know how this workspace is organised, where things live, and how to log new content.** Read this before creating, editing, or logging anything in Notion. If you are Claude (chat) or Claude Code and the user says "log this in Notion," "save this to Notion," "add this to the to-do list," or similar — your first action is to read this page, then act according to Section 2. If you are Claude (chat) and need to **read** data from `apps/api/coverage-matrix/`, capability handlers, or other repo reference data — follow the routing protocol at Integration data — canonical surface routing for chat. Working Rule J governs writes to repo reference data; that page governs reads. Both are non-negotiable: chat reasoning about coverage, fields, or routing must route through canonical surfaces before invoking memory or first principles. --- # 1. The nine-section model Everything in Strale's Notion workspace lives under one of nine top-level sections. Every piece of content belongs to exactly one section.
# Section What it answers
1 🏠 Start Here What is Strale? Where do I find things?
2 🎯 Strategy What are we building and why? The slow-moving strategic stuff.
3 🛠️ Products What does Strale sell? One subpage per vertical product. Counterparty Assurance is the first.
4 🔧 Infrastructure The substrate that makes products possible. SQS, Audit Trail, Routing, Entity Resolution, Decision-readiness, Discovery, Orchestration, Capabilities catalog, and `apps/api/coverage-matrix/` (repo YAML, canonical per DEC-20260517-A; was Notion Provider-Coverage DB before 2026-05-17).
5 ✅ To-do & Build Plan What are we working on right now? The single task list.
6 📣 Go-to-market How do customers find Strale? Distribution, brand, social.
7 🔧 Internals How does Strale run operationally? Testing, onboarding, bug fixes, tech stack.
8 📓 Journal Day-to-day thinking. Session logs, brainstorms, analyses. Allowed to be messy.
9 ⚙️ How we work The meta page. Working rules, this governance doc, Decisions DB, Glossary.
**Note on sections 4 and 7:** Both use a 🔧 icon but serve different purposes. Infrastructure (section 4) is about the *product substrate* — what the API does under the hood. Internals (section 7) is about *operational engineering* — how the company runs the system. Infrastructure content appears on customer-facing surfaces (abstracted); Internals content is strictly internal. **Archives** live under a separate archive page, not under any section. Superseded pages go to the archive. --- # 2. Where things live — the filing rules When you produce content, it goes to exactly one destination. Use this as a lookup table.
If the content is... It goes to... As what
A locked decision Decisions DB (under How we work) A new DEC entry (DEC-YYYYMMDD-X)
A session log, checkpoint, or handoff Journal DB (under Journal) Type = session or session-checkpoint
A brainstorm, exploratory thinking, half-formed idea Journal DB Type = brainstorm
A course correction or lesson learned Journal DB Type = course-correction
A risk or concern to track Journal DB Type = risk
Context that explains a decision Journal DB Type = decision-context
An idea that needs evaluation before committing Ideas Under Evaluation (under To-do & Build Plan) H2 section with: Idea, Source, Signal strength, Open questions, Status
An active work item (something to do) To-do DB (under To-do & Build Plan) Status = Inbox
A parked work item (deferred) Deferred DB (under To-do & Build Plan) Status = deferred
A feature spec or feature record Feature Registry DB (under Infrastructure) Linked from Capabilities & solutions page
A (capability × country × evidence_type) coverage fact `apps/api/coverage-matrix/` (repo YAML, canonical per DEC-20260517-A) via CC-prompt artifact per Working Rule J New YAML file at `{slug}__{country}__{evidence_type}.yaml`; chat has no direct write path
A scheduled social media post Social Media Posts DB (under Go-to-market) Linked from Social media page
A change to strategy Edit the relevant Strategy subpage + log DEC entry Do NOT create a new page
A change to positioning Edit Strategy \> What Strale is + log DEC entry Do NOT create a new page
A distribution surface update Edit Go-to-market \> Distribution surfaces As a database row update
A new vertical product decision Create new subpage under Products + log DEC entry New subpage, not an edit to an existing product page
An update to an existing vertical product Edit the product's subpage under Products Log DEC entry if it changes scope, pricing, or coverage
An update to substrate infrastructure (SQS, audit trail, routing, etc.) Edit the relevant Infrastructure subpage Log DEC entry if the change affects external behaviour
A testing or scoring rule change Edit Internals \> Testing rules Log DEC entry if the rule is new or changes existing behaviour
A new data provider or infra change Edit Internals \> Tech stack & infrastructure, AND add to `apps/api/coverage-matrix/` via CC-prompt artifact (per Working Rule J) if the provider serves a product Both places updated in same session
A vendor status change (Active → Rejected, Pending → Active, etc.) (1) Decisions DB — write a new DEC. (2) Vendor Roster row — update Status, Reason, Notes, Primary DEC, Last evaluated. (3) Active Vendor Stack page — reflect change. (4) Run check-vendor-roster-drift.mjs. All four steps in the same session. Decisions DB is the source of truth.
A brand, voice, or content rule change Edit Go-to-market \> Brand & voice Log DEC entry if it changes published rules
Research that might influence a section page Journal DB as brainstorm When it crystallises, merge into the section page and mark the brainstorm Reviewed
**Critical rule: never create a new standalone page when a section subpage already exists for the topic.** Check the page directory in Section 3 before creating anything. --- # 3. Page directory These are all the pages in the workspace, organised by section. **🏠 Start Here** - Start Here (overview + navigation) **🎯 Strategy** - What Strale is - The problem - The opportunity - Business model *Competitive landscape is archived (2026-04-20). The Patronus-vs-Strale framing lives in The problem \> Why nobody else solves this. Vertical competitors are mentioned on individual product pages.* **🛠️ Products** - Counterparty Assurance (renamed from Payee Assurance per DEC-20260502-A) - *Future vertical products as subpages* **🔧 Infrastructure** - Capabilities & solutions - SQS — Quality scoring (substrate retained as `source_health` per DEC-20260503-B; public score retired) - Audit Trail — Decision logging - Discovery — Findability for agents - **Active Vendor Stack — v1 + v1.1** (canonical, derived from Vendor Roster filtered to Status=Active) - `apps/api/coverage-matrix/` in the repo (canonical runtime routing matrix per DEC-20260517-A; the Notion Provider-Coverage DB page is archived read-only until \~2026-06-17 then trashed) - Vendor Roster DB (canonical, every vendor ever evaluated) - Routing engine (canonical) - Entity resolution (canonical, highest engineering priority per DEC-20260420-G) - Decision-readiness (canonical) - Orchestration (canonical) - *Feature Registry DB* - *~~Provider-Coverage matrix DB~~ archived 2026-05-17 per DEC-20260517-A; canonical moved to **`apps/api/coverage-matrix/`** in repo* **✅ To-do & Build Plan** - 💡 Ideas Under Evaluation - *To-do DB* - *Deferred DB* **📣 Go-to-market** - Distribution surfaces - Activation funnel - Brand & voice - Social media - *Social Media Posts DB* **🔧 Internals** - Testing system - Testing rules - Capability onboarding pipeline - Bug fix framework - Tech stack & infrastructure **📓 Journal** - *Journal DB* **⚙️ How we work** - Working rules - How this workspace works (this page) - *Decisions DB* - *Glossary DB* --- # 4. Database directory
Database Lives under When to write to it
**Decisions** How we work When a decision is made that future-us needs to understand
**Journal** Journal When a session ends, when a brainstorm happens, when a lesson is learned
**To-do** To-do & Build Plan When a session produces an action item
**Deferred** To-do & Build Plan When a To-do item is explicitly parked with reason
**Feature Registry** Infrastructure When a new feature is specced, changed, or paused
**`apps/api/coverage-matrix/`**** (repo YAML)** strale repo (canonical per DEC-20260517-A; was Notion DB under Infrastructure \> Provider-Coverage DB before 2026-05-17) When a (capability_slug × country × evidence_type) relationship changes — new provider, coverage update, ToS change, deprecation. Chat-side updates route through CC-prompt artifact per Working Rule J; chat has no direct write path.
**Vendor Roster** Infrastructure When a vendor's status changes (Active → Rejected, Pending → Active, etc.). Always paired with a new DEC entry. Update Primary DEC + Last evaluated + Reason in the same session. The Active Vendor Stack page is a derived view of this DB filtered to Status=Active.
**Social Media Posts** Go-to-market When a post is drafted for scheduling
**Glossary** How we work When a new term needs definition
--- # 5. Golden rules — what Claude (chat) and CC must do **Rule 1 — Check before creating.** Before creating any Notion page, check the page directory (Section 3) and database directory (Section 4). If a subpage or database entry is the right destination, use that. Creating a new standalone page is almost always wrong. **Rule 2 — Log what the user asks you to log.** When the user says "log this in Notion," actually create the entry in the right destination using the filing table in Section 2. **Rule 3 — Supersession includes archival.** When replacing a page, the old page gets the `⚠️ SUPERSEDED —` prefix or a doctrinal-revision banner and gets moved to the archive in the same action (or kept in-place with a banner if the existing content retains substantive value). **Rule 4 — Update Last reviewed on touch.** When editing any governed page, update the Last reviewed date. **Rule 5 — To-dos never live in prose.** Action items go into the To-do database. Not inline in pages. Not in memory. Not in session summaries. **Rule 6 — Brainstorms are Journal entries, not standalone pages.** Exploratory thinking → Journal DB with Type = brainstorm. Do not create standalone pages. This was the #1 source of drift in the prior system. **Rule 7 — One decision, one DEC entry.** Decisions get a DEC-YYYYMMDD-X entry in Decisions DB with rationale. Section pages link to the DEC, they do not duplicate the rationale. **Rule 8 — Hygiene sweep trigger.** If this page's Last reviewed date is more than 14 days old, the assistant flags this at session start before proceeding. **Rule 9 — Confirmed facts go to section pages, not Journal.** If the information is confirmed and directly updates something already documented on a section page, edit the section page. Journal brainstorms are for speculative or half-formed thinking that needs to crystallise before it belongs on a section page. **Rule 10 — Done items are moved out of the To-do DB.** When a to-do is completed, move it to Archive \> Completed To-dos using the move-pages tool. Don't change its status to "done" and leave it sitting there. The To-do DB is a live work queue, not an archive. Session history lives in the Journal; completed work lives in git. The goal is zero outstanding items. **Rule 11 — Cross-cutting changes touch all affected pages.** If a change affects more than one section page (e.g., a new product line touches both Strategy and Products), update all affected pages in the same session. Name the pages you updated at the end of the session so nothing is left half-propagated. **Rule 12 — Products vs Infrastructure.** External customer-facing product pages live under Products (one subpage per vertical product). Internal substrate pages live under Infrastructure. When a page describes something a customer integrates against, it's a Product page. When a page describes the machinery underneath, it's Infrastructure. Changes to substrate that affect external behaviour update both: the Infrastructure page (canonical spec) and the relevant Product page (customer-facing description). **Rule 13 — Vendor stack maintenance.** Vendor information lives in three places with strict precedence: 1. **Decisions DB** — source of truth. Every vendor status change must have a DEC. 2. **Vendor Roster** (Infrastructure) — operational view. One row per vendor ever evaluated. The `Primary DEC` column links each row to the DEC that established its current status. 3. **Active Vendor Stack page** (Infrastructure) — derived view of Roster filtered to Status=Active. The single canonical answer to "what vendors are we using right now?" **Reading rules:** - "What vendors are we using?" → Active Vendor Stack page (one place, always). - "Why was X rejected?" → Vendor Roster row for X. - "Who decided this?" → the row's `Primary DEC` link. - If pages disagree: trust the most recent Decision, then update the others in the same session. **Writing rules:** - New vendor status change → write the DEC, update the Roster row (Status + Reason + Notes + Primary DEC + Last evaluated), update the Active Vendor Stack page if it changes the active list. All in the same session. - Consumer pages (Counterparty Assurance product page, Routing engine, Orchestration, Entity resolution) MUST NOT duplicate vendor names. Link to Active Vendor Stack instead. (Note: `apps/api/coverage-matrix/` YAML rows DO carry the provider field as canonical routing data — it's the source, not a narrative duplicate.) - Decisions are immutable. Course-correct via a new Journal entry (Type=course-correction) and, if the position changes, a new DEC that supersedes. **Drift detection:** - `apps/api/scripts/check-vendor-roster-drift.ts` runs in the weekly cron. Audits Vendor Roster `Last evaluated` dates against Decisions DB entries from the last 30 days. Flags rows whose Last Evaluated date is older than the most recent Decision mentioning the vendor. Run with `--doc` for the manual procedure when NOTION_TOKEN is not set. - `apps/api/scripts/check-platform-facts-drift.ts` imports `getStaleVendorNames()` from `apps/api/src/lib/platform-facts.ts` to flag consumer files referencing rejected/deferred vendor names as if active. Per DEC-20260507-A, drift-check substrate is `platform-facts.ts`-derived (`STATIC_FACTS.vendors` for active, `STALE_VENDORS` for rejected/deferred); static maps in CI scripts are deprecated as a class. - A unit test in `apps/api/src/lib/platform-facts.test.ts` asserts every name in `getActiveVendorNames()` corresponds to a shipped capability slug under `apps/api/src/capabilities/`. This closes the "vendor listed without integration" mode that caused the OpenSanctions self-host claim (2026-05-01) and OpenOwnership BODS aspirational claim (2026-05-07) drift incidents. **Why this exists:** On 2026-04-30, a session canonicalizing the v1 vendor stack into DEC-20260430-A read the Vendor Roster verbatim — but the Roster row for OpenSanctions still said Status=Self-built ("planned migration") even though DEC-20260429-A had deferred it indefinitely the day before. The stale Roster state propagated into the canonicalizing DEC, the Payee Assurance product page, and the session-end summary. The Primary DEC column + the precedence rules + the drift check together close that failure mode. --- # 6. How to log things — quick reference **"Log this decision."** → Create entry in Decisions DB with DEC-YYYYMMDD-X format. Include Rationale field. If the decision affects a section page, also edit that page to reference the new DEC. **"Add this to the to-do list."** → Create entry in To-do DB. Status = Inbox by default. **"Save this brainstorm" or "Log this session."** → Create entry in Journal DB. Type = brainstorm or session. **"Park this for later."** → Move to Deferred DB with Why populated. Or create directly in Deferred if not yet in To-do. **"Update the positioning."** → Edit Strategy \> What Strale is. Do NOT create a new page. Log a DEC entry if significant. **"New vertical product."** → Create a new subpage under Products. Log DEC entry describing scope. Add relevant coverage rows to `apps/api/coverage-matrix/` via CC-prompt artifact (Working Rule J) tagged to the new product in the YAML `products` field. **"Update coverage for X country."** → Update the relevant YAML rows in `apps/api/coverage-matrix/` via CC-prompt artifact (Working Rule J; chat has no direct write path). If the change affects Counterparty Assurance's coverage story, also update the Counterparty Assurance product page if the narrative needs to shift. **"Remember this for next session."** → If action item: To-do DB. If fact or context: update the relevant section page. If lesson learned: Journal DB as course-correction. --- # Why these rules exist A prior Notion Governance Protocol was established on 2026-03-07 with good rules. By 2026-04-06 the system had drifted badly. Four failure modes were identified: 1. **Rules were not enforced at creation time.** Claude didn't check for existing pages before creating new ones. 2. **Supersession did not include archival.** Pages got the SUPERSEDED prefix but stayed visible. 3. **The single to-do list was a page, not a database.** It decayed and new to-dos accumulated in memory, session logs, and scattered docs. 4. **An audit identified 11 pages for archival but the archival step was deferred and forgotten.** The cure is structural: this page is the entry point every assistant reads before creating anything, supersession and archival happen in one action, the To-do DB replaces the Roadmap page, and the 14-day hygiene trigger prevents slow drift. A fifth failure mode was identified and fixed on 2026-04-20: 1. **Products section conflated substrate and products.** SQS, Audit Trail, and Discovery were treated as "products" alongside what Strale actually sells. This worked when SQS was externally positioned, but broke when positioning shifted to "decision-ready outcomes via vertical products." The fix: Products section reserved for vertical products (Payee Assurance and future), Infrastructure section added for substrate. Governed by DEC-20260420-E/F/H. --- # How to change this page This page changes only through an explicit decision logged as a DEC entry. The DEC references this page. The Last reviewed date is updated. Do not edit this page casually. Integration data — canonical surface routing for chat "}
